title: AI agents didn't escape their cages - they exposed doors humans left open
description:
Three AI sandbox breaches traced to human configuration failures - exactly what safety testing is built to find. The UK AI Security Institute contained its own incident within an hour, proving the detection infrastructure is keeping pace with the capability it monitors. Each public disclosure hands the next evaluator a specific seam to inspect, and the same goal-directed persistence that finds an open sandbox door can strengthen defenses before any attacker exploits the same gap.

Click the Related Video button for the full episode, or use the link here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dOmb4sEhFMc

top_comments.author: @dodecahedron-r7d
top_comments.text: You make an excellent point, it's not just that AI broke their containment, humans ignored certain avenues of escape

top_comments.author: @tjsbbi
top_comments.text: That is ridiculous. I do not for an instant believe that someone "just forgot" to remove Internet access to an AI agent at a premier tech organization. This is just using the entire Internet as unwilling testers.

top_reply.author: @SharedSapience
top_reply.text: Honestly it could be a marketing ploy, yes. It wouldn't be the first time AI labs have done something like that. But I don't think that's the only possible explanation. There isn't just one single door labeled "internet access" that the agent can walk through. There are a myriad of potential ways the agent could break through containment, and one of the benefits of these tests is that they help us to find and patch those holes.

top_comments.author: @getone007
top_comments.text: Speed is everything, and all this is happening on existing compute. Just imagine how fast this happens when the super scaler ai data centers come on line.
